lessons.title: What Is Space Junk and Abandoned Space Hardware?
lessons.overview: When humans explore space, what happens to the machines, equipment and materials they leave behind?

chapters.title: What is space hardware?
chapters.content_text: Space hardware refers to human-made equipment designed, built or used for activities beyond Earth's atmosphere.

chapters.title: What is space junk?
chapters.content_text: The expression space junk is commonly used to describe human-made objects that are no longer useful.

chapters.title: Why is orbital debris a problem?
chapters.content_text:
Spacecraft travel at very high speeds.
Even relatively small pieces of debris can damage spacecraft and create risks for satellites and astronauts.

chapters.title: Why does equipment remain behind?
chapters.content_text: An artifact is an object created, modified or used by humans that has historical, scientific or cultural significance.

lessons.title: The Moon's Forgotten Machines
lessons.overview: What did humanity leave on the Moon, and what can those machines teach us today?

chapters.title: Before Apollo: The first robotic explorers
chapters.content_text:
Human exploration of the Moon did not begin with astronauts.
Before people landed there, robotic spacecraft helped scientists understand the lunar environment.

chapters.title: Apollo: Machines that supported human exploration
chapters.content_text: The Apollo program made it possible for humans to land on the Moon.

chapters.title: The scientific instruments that stayed behind
chapters.content_text:
One of the most important contributions of lunar exploration was the scientific equipment left on the Moon.
Some instruments continued producing valuable scientific information after the astronauts returned to Earth.

chapters.title: What can we still see on the Moon?
chapters.content_text: The lunar surface preserves evidence of historic missions.

chapters.title: Preserving lunar history
chapters.content_text: The Moon has no ordinary weather system like Earth.

lessons.title: Mars: The Robots That Stayed Behind
lessons.overview: How did robotic explorers investigate Mars, what did they discover, and what happened to the machines after their missions?

chapters.title: The different types of Mars explorers
chapters.content_text: Mars exploration uses three major types of robotic spacecraft.

chapters.title: The early Mars explorers
chapters.content_text:
Before modern rovers, engineers had to solve a fundamental problem:
Could a spacecraft survive the journey to Mars and successfully reach its surface?

chapters.title: Perseverance: Searching for evidence of ancient life
Ingenuity: The first powered aircraft on another planet
chapters.content_text: Mars exploration also introduced an entirely different type of robotic machine.

chapters.title: The machines that stopped working
chapters.content_text: Not every Mars mission remains active forever.

chapters.title: How do Mars robots communicate with Earth?
chapters.content_text: A Mars rover cannot simply use an ordinary mobile-phone network.

chapters.title: How do robots land on Mars?
chapters.content_text: Landing a spacecraft on Mars is one of the most challenging parts of a mission.

chapters.title: The future of Mars exploration
chapters.content_text: Mars exploration continues to develop.

lessons.title: How Does Space Hardware Work?
lessons.overview: How can a machine survive in space, move through the universe, communicate with Earth and perform scientific investigations without human hands operating it directly?

chapters.title: Understanding the spacecraft as a system
chapters.content_text: Before studying individual components, we need to understand how a spacecraft is organized.

chapters.title: Electrical power systems
chapters.content_text: Every electronic spacecraft system requires electrical power.

chapters.title: Communication systems
chapters.content_text: How does a spacecraft send photographs from another planet?

chapters.title: Guidance, Navigation and Control
chapters.content_text: A spacecraft must know where it is, which direction it is facing and how to maintain its intended orientation.

chapters.title: Propulsion systems
chapters.content_text: A spacecraft sometimes needs to change its velocity or trajectory.

chapters.title: Thermal-control systems
chapters.content_text: Spacecraft operate in environments with significant temperature variations.

chapters.title: Command, computers and data handling
chapters.content_text: A spacecraft requires computers to coordinate its operations.

chapters.title: Scientific instruments and payloads
chapters.content_text: A spacecraft can have excellent power, communication and navigation systems, but without a useful scientific payload, it cannot achieve its intended scientific objectives.

chapters.title: Structures and mechanical systems
chapters.content_text: A spacecraft needs a physical structure that supports its equipment and protects important components.

chapters.title: Autonomous systems
chapters.content_text: Some spacecraft must perform tasks without receiving instructions for every individual movement.

chapters.title: How all spacecraft systems work together
chapters.content_text: Understanding individual components is useful, but understanding their interactions is what makes someone think like a spacecraft engineer.

chapters.content_text:

Unexpected discoveries.

chapters.content_text:

lessons.title: Why Does Space Equipment Get Abandoned?
lessons.overview:
That lesson will connect mission design, engineering limitations, scientific priorities and the reasons hardware remains in space.
If a spacecraft costs millions or billions to build and launch, why don't we bring it back when its mission ends?

chapters.title: Spacecraft do not last forever
chapters.content_text: Why spacecraft have limited lifetimes?

chapters.title: Why missions come to an end
chapters.content_text: Investigate six major causes.

chapters.title: What happens after a mission ends?

lessons.title: Engineering Behind Space Hardware.
lessons.overview:
This will take learners beyond understanding spacecraft components and introduce the engineering decisions, constraints, trade-offs and innovations that make space exploration possible.
How do engineers build machines that must work in space, often millions of kilometres away, where repair may be impossible?

lessons.title: Analyze a Space Mission and Its Scientific Data.
lessons.overview: This will introduce learners to the work of researchers: examining real mission observations, interpreting data, identifying patterns and building conclusions supported by evidence.

lessons.title: Future of Space Technology and Space Sustainability.
lessons.overview:
This final flagship lesson will connect the entire curriculum to future exploration, responsible space operations, sustainability, innovation and the role learners can play in shaping humanity's future in space.
How can humanity continue exploring space while protecting the environments, scientific opportunities and resources that make exploration possible?
